In particular, almost all steps of our algorithm work if each v ∈ V uses colors {1, 2, . . . , d(v) e + 1}, for d(v) e a locally computable upper bound on degrees. It would be interesting to know if d(v) + 1-coloring could be solved. The more e difficult list variants of this problem, where nodes must adopt colors from lists of size ∆2 + 1 or d(v) e + 1, are also open. Key aspects of our approach fail for list coloring and, in fact, it is not even known if ∆ + 1-list-coloring of G is achievable in poly log log n rounds of broadcast CONGEST. It would also be interesting to push the complexity of ∆2 + 1-coloring of G2 down to O(log∗ n) when ∆ ≥ poly log n, to fully match the state of the art at distance one. While we conjecture that minor modifications to our algorithm1 might be able to reduce its complexity by one or more log log n factors, achieving O(log∗ n) would require a new approach, as many steps of our algorithm use Ω(log log ∆) rounds.
